subject: Week 40: 50% walk by 12 months, 90% by 15 — pad the landing zone
bodyText:
This week
Days 278 through 284 open the final quarter, and walking is now the dominant motor question: roughly 50% of infants walk by 12 months, 75% by 14, and 90% by 15. The CDC moved its walks-alone checkpoint to 15 months in the 2022 revision, so a non-walker at the first birthday sits squarely inside the distribution. Expect fluid cruising, brief unsupported stands for some (CDC checkpoint: 12 months), and more elaborate imitation — stirring with a spoon, pushing a car across the floor.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Several falls a day during practice. The target is supervised falls onto forgiving surfaces, not zero falls.
- [low concern] Head bonks against furniture edges — the fall is not the hazard, the corner is; pad the coffee table and the hearth this week.
- [monitor] Persistent inability to bear weight through his legs when you hold him upright — this one goes to the pediatrician directly rather than into the notes file.
- [call within 24h] New wheezing, or an illness that plateaus instead of improving — RSV and influenza run through March here.
- [call now] Head injury followed by persistent vomiting, unusual lethargy, or any loss of consciousness; fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy; labored breathing or blue lips — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Re-audit the house at standing height: pad the hearth and coffee-table corners, add window guards on anything above ground level (screens are not weight-bearing), and put pinch guards on doors he can swing shut. The last audit was run for a baby who could not reach a tabletop. AAP: Childproofing Your Home: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-home/Pages/Childproofing-Your-Home.aspx
- Practice stairs upward with you seated one step behind him — two or three carpeted steps, up only, daily. Stair climbing trains the same hip and ankle control walking needs, and it is the skill that prevents the fall down them later. AAP: Movement 8 to 12 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
- Hand him the real object instead of the toy version — a soft brush for his own hair, a wooden spoon in an empty bowl, a cloth for his tray. Using objects for their intended purpose is the CDC 12-month cognitive item, and copying your actual routines is how he gets there. CDC 1-year milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Write the sick-day plan down before you need it: who takes the fever call, which backup-care benefit you actually have, and the 24-hour fever-free return rule most centers run. Infants in group care average 8 to 12 illnesses in year one, at a parental cost of roughly five to 10 missed workdays. AAP: Fever: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/fever/Pages/default.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — the window closes Monday. If the visit happened, the only open items should be the iron result and influenza #2; if it did not, call Monday morning and take a late slot.
- Day 285-291 (Feb 20-26, 2027): first outdoor shoes become relevant if he is walking outside — flexible soles only, and barefoot stays the indoor default.
- Day 364-380 (May 10-26, 2027): 12-month well visit — the next scheduled well visit once Monday's window closes.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Plays peekaboo (initiates by covering and uncovering face)
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Active game initiation, not just smiling when you hide. Demonstrates object permanence in action.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/plays-peekaboo/complete

- Plays games like pat-a-cake
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Imitative gesture game. Joint attention + motor imitation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/plays-pat-a-cake/complete

- Waves bye-bye
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Intentional gesture with social meaning.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/waves-bye/complete

- Calls a parent 'mama' or 'dada' or another name
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Specifically referring to a person, not generalized babble. First true word for many babies.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calls-parent-by-name/complete

- Understands 'no' (pauses or stops when you say it)
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Receptive language. Compliance is a much later milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/understands-no/complete
